digest.top_line: SARON: consolidation RT added to 1L SACT in synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC, mOS 31.0 vs 28.0mo (HR 0.99, p=0.95) despite mPFS HR 0.64.
digest.tldr: Two RT-backbone trials missed their primary endpoints. In SARON, consolidation RT cut 12-mo local failure (13.0% vs 39.5%) and improved mPFS (HR 0.64) but not OS in synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC. KEYNOTE-975 showed no EFS gain from concurrent pembro + dCRT in esophageal/GEJ cancer with CPS ≥10 (HR 0.97). Thoracic and upper GI lead.

sites.intro: Concurrent pembro + dCRT is negative at IA2 in CPS ≥10. Consolidation-timed IO after dCRT remains untested.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-975
studies.tldr: EFS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.77-1.23), median 15.2 vs 14.7 mo in PD-L1 CPS ≥10: no EFS gain adding concurrent pembro to dCRT in unresectable esophageal/GEJ cancer.

details.text: 📊 Dual-primary endpoints in PD-L1 CPS ≥10 at IA2 (pembro + dCRT vs pbo + dCRT)

details: 📐 Hierarchical testing: EFS in CPS ≥10 failed, so CPS ≥1, all-pt EFS and OS went untested
🔍 Study stopped after IA2; median f/u 47.1 mo (range 21.7-70.2), data cut-off Jan 21, 2026
💊 Pembro 200 mg Q3W ×8 cycles, then 400 mg Q6W ×5 cycles, concurrent with dCRT

subdetails: Fractionation and target volume not reported in source

details: ⚠️ RT dose (50 vs 60 Gy) and chemo backbone were by site choice; no outcome split by dose in source
⚠️ ESCC and EAC/GEJ pooled; histology-specific results not reported in source
⚠️ No local control or patterns-of-failure data in source
🔗 Concurrent IO from CRT start, not PACIFIC-style consolidation after CRT; timing question untested here

verdict.rationale: Double-blind phase 3 stopped at IA2 after the gatekeeper EFS endpoint failed in the enriched CPS ≥10 group; reaffirms dCRT alone as standard. Downstream populations formally untested.
verdict.audience: Untreated unresectable locally advanced ESCC/EAC/GEJ, dCRT candidates

studies.significance: The trial failed in the enriched PD-L1 CPS ≥10 group, where IO was most likely to help, and the curves sat on top of each other (EFS HR 0.97, OS HR 1.00) at 47.1 mo median f/u. Grade 5 AEs ran 13% vs 10%, so concurrent pembro with 50-60 Gy dCRT adds toxicity without benefit. This leaves dCRT alone as the backbone.
studies.monday_clinic: In untreated unresectable esophageal or GEJ cancer going to dCRT, including PD-L1 CPS ≥10, this does not support concurrent pembrolizumab; it does not address consolidation-only IO after dCRT or the resectable trimodality setting.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: International **phase 3, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled**, multicenter; **N=703**. Results are from the **second interim analysis (IA2)**, after which the study was stopped. Median follow-up 47.1 mo.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Previously untreated **locally advanced unresectable** ESCC, EAC or GEJ cancer (cTX N+ M0 or cT2-T4a NX M0), or cervical/upper thoracic EC with **supraclavicular nodal M1 only**. ECOG 0-1, **ineligible for curative surgery but suitable for dCRT**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Pembro 200 mg or placebo Q3W for 8 cycles, then 400 mg or placebo Q6W for 5 cycles, **concurrent** with dCRT. Chemo backbone FP or FOLFOX by site choice.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **50 Gy or 60 Gy** with FP, or **50 Gy** with FOLFOX, by site choice. Fractionation, technique and target volume not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Dual primary:** investigator-assessed EFS and OS, tested hierarchically in PD-L1 CPS ≥10, CPS ≥1, then all pts.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **EFS not improved** in CPS ≥10 (arm-level numbers in table), so every downstream comparison went untested and the study was stopped.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Grade ≥3 AEs in **100%** of both arms. Grade 5 AEs **44 (13%) vs 37 (10%)**, AE discontinuation **117 (34%) vs 97 (27%)**. Authors report no new safety signals.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Joins KUNLUN (durvalumab + dCRT) as a negative concurrent IO-dCRT trial in esophageal cancer. Adjuvant nivolumab per CheckMate 577 belongs to the resected trimodality setting and is untouched by this result.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents untreated unresectable locally advanced esophageal/GEJ cancer treated with concurrent pembro and 50-60 Gy dCRT. Does not represent consolidation-only IO after dCRT or resectable trimodality pts.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: RT dose and chemo backbone by site choice with no outcome breakdown, pooled histologies, and no local control or failure-pattern data in source to show whether IO changed in-field control.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: A flat EFS and OS in the PD-L1-enriched group argues against a hidden benefit in the untested CPS ≥1 or all-comer groups. Whether timing (consolidation vs concurrent) or histology matters stays open.

studies.interpretation:
The most informative thing about KEYNOTE-975 is where it failed. The sponsor put the PD-L1 CPS ≥10 population first in the testing hierarchy, the group where checkpoint inhibition had the best chance of showing benefit, and the EFS hazard ratio was 0.97 with an interval reaching from 0.77 to 1.23. OS in the same group was HR 1.00. Formally, the CPS ≥1 and all-comer comparisons were never tested. In practice, a null result in the enriched group makes a real benefit in a diluted population hard to believe. With median follow-up of 47.1 months, this is no premature look that could still turn: it is a mature negative read, stopped at the second interim analysis.

It also fits what the field already had. KUNLUN tested durvalumab with dCRT in the same broad setting and also failed to show an EFS benefit, so two placebo-controlled programs with different PD-(L)1 agents now agree. The hope behind both came partly from PACIFIC in stage III NSCLC, but PACIFIC gave durvalumab as consolidation after chemoradiation was finished. Here pembrolizumab started with dCRT and continued alongside it. KEYNOTE-975 therefore answers the concurrent question and leaves the sequencing question open. A reader should not assume consolidation would behave the same way, and should also not assume it would succeed where concurrent dosing did not. No randomized evidence in this source speaks to it.

For a radiation oncologist, the RT-specific gaps matter. Dose (50 or 60 Gy) and backbone (FP or FOLFOX) were left to each site, and the source gives no results by dose, no local control, and no in-field versus distant failure pattern. One mechanistic hope for adding IO to RT is better locoregional control through immune priming, and this abstract cannot confirm or refute that. A trial can be EFS-negative and still move local control, and we cannot tell here. The pooling of squamous and adenocarcinoma histologies is a second blind spot, since these behave differently and respond differently to IO in other settings. A benefit restricted to ESCC with high PD-L1, offset by none elsewhere, would look much like this, though the CPS ≥10 result makes a large hidden effect unlikely.

The safety numbers deserve more weight than the authors' "no new safety signals" suggests. Grade 5 events were 44 (13%) versus 37 (10%), and AE-driven discontinuation was 117 (34%) versus 97 (27%). Given no efficacy return, that is a cost with no benefit attached. A grade ≥3 rate of 100% in both arms is unusual and likely reflects how events were counted over a long follow-up, which the full paper should clarify.

The decision it settles: dCRT without concurrent PD-1 blockade stays the standard for unresectable esophageal and GEJ cancer, regardless of PD-L1 status. The decisions it leaves open: consolidation timing, histology-specific effects, and whether any RT parameter interacts with IO. The result would only be wrong if a benefit sat in a subgroup this hierarchy never tested and the CPS ≥10 cut failed to enrich for it, and the data give little reason to expect that.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Concurrent pembro with 50-60 Gy dCRT did not move EFS (HR 0.97) or OS (HR 1.00) in CPS ≥10 pts, and grade 5 AEs rose to 13% vs 10%. No local control or dose-stratified data in source, so the RT backbone stays dCRT alone with no IO-driven change to dose or volume.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: PD-L1 CPS ≥10 enrichment did not rescue concurrent pembro (EFS HR 0.97, OS HR 1.00), and AE discontinuation rose to 34% vs 27%. Biomarker selection does not justify adding PD-1 blockade to dCRT; consolidation-only timing remains untested by this trial.

open_questions: Would consolidation-only IO after dCRT differ from concurrent dosing?
Histology-specific EFS in ESCC vs EAC/GEJ
Did pembro alter local control or failure patterns?

sites.intro: SARON's OS-null result in oligometastatic NSCLC arrives with a clear local-failure and PFS benefit from consolidation RT.

studies.name: SARON
studies.tldr: Consolidation RT added to 1L SACT: mOS 31.0 vs 28.0mo (HR 0.99, p=0.95) despite mPFS 13.9 vs 8.9mo (HR 0.64) in synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC.

details.text: 📊 SACT+RT vs SACT alone, median f/u 37.4mo

details: 🔍 Randomised (1:1) phase II, N=140, 22 UK centres, accrual Oct 2016 to Jul 2023
🔍 1-5 metastases in ≤3 organs, AGA-negative; randomised after initial SACT with CR/PR/SD

subdetails: Radical RT to lung primary ± locoregional nodes

details: 🔍 62.9% had 1 OM site; 52.9% N2/3; 6.4% brain mets
💊 SACT: 40.0% chemo, 15.0% IO, 45.0% chemo-IO; control arm added IO Jan 2020
📊 6 pts had G3 events possibly RT-related; QLQ-C30/LC13 QoL similar between arms
🔗 vs Gomez LCT phase II: OS 41.2 vs 17.0mo there, but n=49 and pre-IO era
⚠️ OS-powered with N=140 in phase II: a modest OS effect cannot be excluded (CI to 0.63)
⚠️ Mixed systemic backbone across eras; only 60% received any IO
⚠️ Post-progression salvage RT in control arm not reported in source; may dilute OS

verdict.rationale: Randomised, completed analysis with OS as stated primary and null result, diverging from prior small LCT trial OS signal. Phase II size leaves OS CI wide.
verdict.audience: Synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC, 1-5 mets, non-progressing on 1L SACT

studies.significance: Pattern of failure is the RT read: 12-mo local failure fell 39.5% to 13.0%, but new distant mets ran 36.2% vs 32.3%. Comprehensive RT controls what it treats without changing systemic seeding, so consolidation in AGA-negative oligometastatic NSCLC is a PFS and local-control decision, not a survival claim.
studies.monday_clinic: In synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC stable or responding on 1L SACT, this supports consolidation RT for local control and PFS when lesions threaten morbidity; it does not support counselling a survival gain, and it does not address EGFR/ALK-positive disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicentre **randomised (1:1) phase II**, N=140 across 22 UK centres, Oct 2016 to Jul 2023. Stratified by SACT, histology, N-stage, number of metastases, brain mets and site. Median follow-up **37.4 mo**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC**, 1-5 metastases in ≤3 organs, all sites amenable to SABR/SRS, randomised after initial SACT with CR, PR or SD. Median age 68, 58.6% adenocarcinoma, 52.9% N2/3, 62.9% a single OM site.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: SACT was 40.0% chemo, 15.0% IO and 45.0% chemo-IO; the control arm changed to include IO in January 2020. Median SACT cycles was 4 in both arms, with maintenance permitted.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Radical RT to the lung primary ± locoregional nodes** plus **SABR to all OM sites**. 62/70 (88.6%) received RT: 51 conventional and 11 SABR to the primary, 54 SABR to ≥1 OM site. Dose and fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **OS.** Major secondary: PFS. Also reported: cumulative incidence of local failure and new distant metastasis, AEs, EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G≥3 AE rate **28.6% in both arms**; 6 pts had a G3 event possibly RT-related. QoL similar between arms.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The Gomez LCT phase II reported OS 41.2 vs 17.0 mo, but in 49 pts before routine IO. SABR-COMET supported the oligometastatic paradigm with few lung primaries. SARON is the larger NSCLC-specific randomised test and **does not reproduce the OS benefit**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC with 1-5 mets in ≤3 organs, non-progressing on 1L SACT. Does not represent AGA-positive disease, metachronous or oligoprogressive disease, or a uniformly chemo-IO-treated population.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Systemic backbone shifted mid-accrual, so the RT effect on a uniform chemo-IO backbone is not isolated. Post-progression therapy, including salvage RT in the control arm, is not reported in source and could compress OS.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: RT did what it was aimed at: local failure fell and PFS improved, while new distant metastasis was **unchanged**. The OS null points to systemic relapse as the limiting event, so lesion count alone selects poorly for the pts in whom ablation alters natural history.

studies.interpretation:
SARON is the first NSCLC-specific randomised trial of this size to test consolidation RT in synchronous oligometastatic disease with OS as the stated endpoint, and its answer is split. The local-therapy hypothesis holds where RT acts: cumulative incidence of local failure within 12 months was 13.0% vs 39.5%, and mPFS 13.9 vs 8.9 mo (HR 0.64). It does not hold where the oligometastatic argument has always made its larger claim. OS was 31.0 vs 28.0 mo with an HR of 0.99, and new distant metastases appeared at 36.2% vs 32.3%. The trial treated visible disease well and left the rate of new seeding untouched.

That pattern is the most informative part of the result, more than the OS point estimate. A survival benefit from consolidation requires either that the treated lesions were the main source of later dissemination, or that preventing local progression spares pts the morbidity and treatment breaks that shorten survival. The distant-metastasis curves argue against the first mechanism in this population. Most pts who progressed did so at new sites that no RT field would have covered.

Against prior data, the contrast with the Gomez LCT trial is the obvious one. That study's OS of 41.2 vs 17.0 mo came from 49 pts in a pre-IO setting and has carried a lot of the enthusiasm for comprehensive consolidation. A small trial with a large OS effect is exactly the result most likely to shrink on replication, and SARON is a reasonable test of that. Still, SARON is not a definitive refutation. With 140 pts in a phase II design the OS confidence interval runs from 0.63 to 1.55, which is compatible with a clinically meaningful benefit as well as with harm. The fair statement is that SARON gives no evidence of an OS effect, not that it proves there is none.

Two design features should temper confidence in the null as well. First, the systemic backbone changed during accrual: only 60% received any IO, and the control arm moved to IO in January 2020. If consolidation is most valuable in pts whose micrometastatic disease is controlled by durable checkpoint response, a chemo-heavy cohort is the wrong place to find that. Second, post-progression therapy is not reported in the source. Control-arm pts who progressed locally may have received salvage RT, which would convert an upfront-versus-deferred comparison into something close to a timing question and push OS together.

For the RT reader the practical consequence is a change in the counselling frame rather than the abandonment of consolidation. Toxicity was not increased overall (G≥3 28.6% both arms, 6 pts with G3 events possibly RT-related) and QoL was similar, so local control and PFS remain defensible goals, particularly for a primary or nodal mass likely to cause symptoms. What SARON removes is the license to describe comprehensive RT as life-prolonging in unselected AGA-negative oligometastatic NSCLC. The trial would be wrong in its OS conclusion if a uniformly chemo-IO-treated, response-selected cohort, or one enriched by ctDNA clearance, showed a survival effect that the heterogeneous SARON population diluted. That is the question the next trial should be built around, rather than another count-based eligibility rule.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 12-mo local failure fell 39.5% to 13.0% with radical RT to primary ± nodes plus SABR to all OM sites, while new distant mets were unchanged (36.2% vs 32.3%). Consolidation is justified on local control and PFS; dose and fractionation are not reported in source, so technique transfer is unverified.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The OS null (HR 0.99) arose on a mixed backbone: 40.0% chemo, 15.0% IO, 45.0% chemo-IO, with IO added to control mid-trial. Whether consolidation adds survival on uniform 1L chemo-IO remains untested, so referral for RT is a PFS decision, not a survival one.

open_questions: Does consolidation RT add OS on a uniform chemo-IO backbone?
Can ctDNA or systemic response select pts who gain OS from consolidation?
How much did control-arm salvage RT compress the OS difference?

papers.title: Pembrolizumab or placebo plus concurrent definitive chemoradiotherapy in esophageal and gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) cancer: The phase 3 randomized KEYNOTE-975 study
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2875O · Proffered paper 1: Gastrointestinal tumour, upper digestive · 2026-10-23 · presented by Manish A. Shah (New York, United States of America) · NCT04210115

Background: The role of immunotherapy in participants (pts) with locally advanced, esophageal cancer (EC) treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) is not established. KEYNOTE-975 (NCT04210115) is an international phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo (pbo) controlled multicenter study that examines dCRT ± pembro in pts with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable esophageal and GEJ cancer. We report results from the second interim analysis (IA2).
Methods: Eligible pts with histologically confirmed cTX N+ M0 or cT2-T4a NX M0 esophageal squamous cell cancer (ESCC) or adenocarcinoma (EAC) or GEJ cancer, or cTX N+ M1 cervical or upper thoracic EC with supraclavicular lymph node metastases only, ECOG PS 0-1, and who were ineligible for curative surgery but suitable for dCRT, were randomized 1:1 to 200 mg pembro or pbo Q3W for 8 cycles then 400 mg pembro or pbo Q6W for 5 cycles + site choice of dCRT (5-fluorouracil + cisplatin [FP] with radiotherapy [RT] 50 Gy or 60 Gy, or FOLFOX with RT 50 Gy). Dual-primary endpoints were event-free survival (EFS) by investigator and OS in pts with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) ≥10, CPS ≥1, and all pts. Data cut-off was Jan 21, 2026.
Results: A total of 703 pts were randomized (349 pembro + dCRT; 354 pbo + dCRT). Median follow-up was 47.1 mo (range, 21.7-70.2) in all pts. At IA2, in pts with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, EFS was not improved with pembro + dCRT vs pbo + dCRT (median 15.2 vs 14.7 mo; HR 0.97; 95% CI, 0.77-1.23 [P=0.3994; P-value boundary for significance 0.0193). In pts with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, median OS was 32.2 mo vs 35.0 mo (HR 1.00; 95% CI, 0.77-1.30 [nominal P-value 0.5003]). As EFS was not positive in PD-L1 CPS ≥10, EFS in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and all pts, and OS were not tested for statistical significance, and the study was stopped. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 100% of pts in each arm, with grade 5 AEs in 44 (13%) vs 37 (10%) pts. Discontinuation due to any AE occurred in 117 (34%) vs 97 (27%) pts.
Conclusions: Pembrolizumab + dCRT vs pbo + dCRT did not significantly improve EFS in untreated unresectable esophageal or GEJ cancer with PD-L1 CPS ≥10. No new safety signals were observed.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04210115.

papers.title: Primary results of SARON: A randomised-controlled trial of consolidation radiotherapy for synchronous oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2613O · Proffered paper 1: NSCLC, metastatic · 2026-10-25 · presented by Fiona McDonald (London, United Kingdom) · NCT02417662

Background: Standard first-line systemic anti-cancer therapy (SACT) for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable genomic alteration (AGA-negative) is chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy. We investigated whether patients with synchronous oligometastatic (OM) AGA-negative NSCLC benefit from the addition of consolidation radiotherapy (RT).
Methods: SARON, a multicentre phase II trial, randomised (1:1) patients with NSCLC, 1–5 metastases in ≤3 organs, to SACT with or without radical RT. The control arm changed to include immunotherapy in January 2020. The experimental arm received radical RT to the lung primary ± locoregional lymph nodes, and stereotactic ablative RT (SABR) to OM sites. Stratification included SACT, histology, N-stage, number of metastases, brain metastases and recruiting site. Primary and major secondary endpoints were overall (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS).
Results: 140 patients were randomised across 22 UK centres (October 2016 to July 2023). Median age was 68 years (range 45–85), 59.3% male, 58.6% adenocarcinoma, 52.9% N-stage 2/3, 62.9% 1x OM site (23.6% 2x, 9.3% 3x, 3.6% 4x, 0.7% 5x OM sites), and 6.4% brain metastases. SACT was 40.0% chemotherapy, 15.0% immunotherapy and 45.0% combination. Median SACT cycles received in both arms was 4, and 62/70 (88.6%) received RT (51 conventional and 11 SABR to primary, 54 SABR to ≥1 OM site). After 37.4 months median follow-up, median OS was 31.0 versus 28.0 months (HR=0.99, 95%CI 0.63–1.55, p=0.95) and median PFS 13.9 versus 8.9 months (HR=0.64, 95%CI 0.43–0.95, p=0.03) in the SACT+RT and SACT arms, respectively. The cumulative incidence of local failure within 12 months was 13.0% versus 39.5% (p<0.01), compared to 36.2% versus 32.3% (p=0.28) for new distant metastasis, respectively. The grade ≥3 adverse event rate was 28.6% in both arms; 6 patients had a grade 3 event possibly related to RT. EORTC QLQ-C30 and LC13 quality of life measures were similar in both arms.
Conclusions: Patients with synchronous OM AGA-negative NSCLC receiving first-line SACT+RT achieved better local disease control and longer PFS than SACT alone with acceptable side-effects, however, this did not translate into survival benefit.
Clinical trial identification: NCT02417662.

papers.title: Towards organ preservation and cure via immunotherapy in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma patients, normally undergoing extensive curative surgery and radiotherapy (MATISSE 2)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2486RO · Rapid oral: Melanoma and other skin tumours · 2026-10-25 · presented by Stan W. Van Dijk (Amsterdam, Netherlands) · NCT06823479

Background: The MATISSE trial (NCT04620200) showed that 80% of patients with a cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) and an indication for extensive curative surgery with or without adjuvant radiotherapy as standard of care (SOC) reached a partial or major pathological response following two courses of neoadjuvant nivolumab and ipilimumab (NIVO/IPI). In addition, 9 patients reached a clinical complete remission (CCR) after only two courses of NIVO/IPI, without SOC. This raised the question whether organ preservation and cure can be reached via only ultra-short neoadjuvant NIVO/IPI, without SOC and without maintenance immunotherapy.
Methods: In the MATISSE 2 trial (NCT06823479), 41 CSCC patients with an indication for extensive or disfiguring curative surgery will be treated with neoadjuvant NIVO (weeks 0 & 2) and IPI (only week 0). Response evaluation is performed in week 5. In case of a non-response, patients undergo SOC in week 6. In case of a clinical response following NIVO/IPI, we will withhold SOC and patients enter a strict wait-and-monitoring programme.
Results: So far, thirty-one patients have been included (median follow-up of 8 months). Overall, 22/31 (71%) patients showed a clinical response in week 5 and did not undergo SOC per protocol, of whom 15/31 (48%) achieved a CCR and 7/31 (23%) achieved a partial clinical response (PCR) during their wait-and-monitoring program. In total 9/31 (29%) patients received SOC, of whom one patient showed a complete pathological response in the surgical specimen. Immune-related toxicity (19% grade 3-4) was well manageable. There was no delay in surgery due to immune-related toxicity.
Conclusions: Overall, 71% of patients reached a clinical response and did not undergo surgery. So far, 48% of patients reached a CCR following only ultra-short neoadjuvant NIVO/IPI, without SOC and without maintenance immunotherapy. Longer follow-up is required to investigate further deepening of the response in PCR patients and the durability of the response in CCR patients.
Clinical trial identification: NCT06823479 EU trial nr 2024-516152-17-00.

papers.title: Cohort level safety and efficacy results for [212Pb]VMT-a-NET in advanced somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2+)-expressing neuroendocrine tumors (NETs): Cohorts 1–3
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2396RO · Rapid oral: NETs and endocrine tumours · 2026-10-23 · presented by Thorvardur R. Halfdanarson (Rochester, United States of America) · NCT05636618

Background: [212Pb]VMT-a-NET is an alpha-particle radiopharmaceutical targeting somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2)-expressing tumors. We present safety and efficacy results from the dose-escalation phase 1/2a clinical trial (NCT05636618).
Methods: Eligible participants (pt) for this study must have unresectable or metastatic NETs, documented radiologic progression following at least 1 prior systemic treatment, and evidence of SSTR2 expression in ≥1 lesion confirmed on an FDA approved SSTR PET scan. During the dose finding phase, pts may receive up to 4 administrations of [212Pb]VMT-a-NET at their assigned dose level, and they are monitored for dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) for 42 days and safety throughout the study. Efficacy is evaluated by investigators according to RECIST criteria v1.1.
Results: As of 03Apr2026, 67 pts have been enrolled in the study and received at least 1 dose of [212Pb]VMT-α-NET: 2 pts in dose Cohort 1 (2.5 mCi), 46 in Cohort 2 (5 mCi), and 19 in Cohort 3 (6 mCi). No DLTs, Grade 4 or 5 adverse events, treatment-related discontinuations, serious renal events, dysphagia, or clinically significant treatment-related myelosuppression have been observed. Efficacy evaluation was previously performed and presented for cohort 1 and a subset of pts of cohort 2 (n=23/46) who had sufficient duration of follow up (96.4 wks and 60.1 wks, respectively) and an ORR in cohort 2 of 43.4%. The presented efficacy set will include 56 pts (n=2 in Cohorts 1, n=46 in 2, and n= 8 in Cohort 3). Among the DLT Cohort 3, 2 pts achieved a PR after 1 and 2 cycles. Both pts in Cohort 1 continued to exhibit stable disease after 2 years of follow up.
Conclusions: Treatment with [212Pb]VMT-α-NET demonstrates a favorable safety profile across all treated pts (n=67) and shows signs of sustained efficacy at the 2.5, 5, and 6 mCi dose levels. The therapy is well tolerated with no observed dose-limiting toxicities or serious treatment-related adverse events. This study is ongoing and enrolling into Cohort 4.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05636618.
